disposition_reason: The original spike-rate inference endpoint is recoverable, but the exact full retrained-CASCADE correlation baseline, source-era timing/configurations and per-condition panel are not yet bound. Approximate cortical-default performance or a later timing repair cannot serve as the improvement target.

source_paper.title: Spike Rate Inference from Mouse Spinal Cord Calcium Imaging Data

evidence.locator: Methods: Quantification of spike rate inference performance and Spike rate inference with CASCADE and OASIS; Figure 4d–h
evidence.supports: Original DS40/41 task, leave-one-neuron-out fitting, sampling/noise settings, smoothing and comparison conditions.
Current author LOO route, neuron exclusion, preprocessing, correlation/error/bias formulas and summary policies; not proof of historical figure equivalence.
The registered source advertises a 44-cell construction scope but has no qualified executed author comparison or selected scientific runtime; these are registration facts, not paper validation.

target.description: Infer continuous, smoothed spike rates from spinal-cord calcium fluorescence against paired electrophysiology. Discrete-spike detection and in-vivo denoising are different endpoints.

dataset.description: CASCADE ground-truth datasets DS40 and DS41, as linked by the paper; exact archival bytes and paper code configuration remain to be bound.

cohort.description: Figure 4d–e specifies 21 glutamatergic and 23 GABAergic spinal neurons. Preserve both populations and each original condition; cortex is a separate comparator dataset.

split.description: Within-dataset retraining excludes the test neuron, including its recordings, for every evaluated neuron. Cross-dataset and cortical-default models remain distinct comparators.

inputs.description: Extracted calcium ΔF/F traces; paired electrical spikes provide targets, never candidate inputs.

preprocessing.description: Paper Figure 4d–f uses 30 Hz, standardized noise 7 and 50 ms Gaussian target smoothing; other conditions have different kernels. Recover exact resampling/noise realizations, edge handling and source-era dataset-wide delay correction. The current demo noise grid 2,4,6,8 is not this original grid.

metric.description: Pearson correlation of inferred and target spike-rate traces, higher is better. Error and signed bias must remain separate diagnostics rather than a new composite score.

aggregation.description: Original figure boxplots summarize per-neuron results separately by cell type and condition. The current demo additionally pools noise rows; that pooled summary is not the paper estimator.

comparison.primary_metric: Per-neuron spike-rate correlation summarized by the original cell-type and sampling/noise panels

published_baseline.description: The paper gives approximate pooled default-CASCADE correlation (~0.47) and relative retraining effects, not the exact complete retrained-CASCADE baseline vector recovered here. Those approximations, p-values and default-model numbers are not the source-paper result to beat.

reproduced_author_baseline.description: No qualified rerun of the original author comparison is established. Public source and construction code are a recovery route, not a measured comparator.

minimum_effect.rationale: A meaningful effect must be justified for this original endpoint after recovering its numerical baseline and measurement variability; no generic percentage or significance-only victory is admitted.

uncertainty.method: Predeclare paired uncertainty for the complete original panel after recovering source-level dependence and replication; no final decision rule is yet qualified.
uncertainty.independent_unit: Paired neurons with all recordings/noise replicas grouped; animal/session clustering must be resolved. Time bins, segments and artificial-noise replicas are not independent biological samples.
uncertainty.rationale: Changing the evaluation partition to simplify inference would define a separate extension.

paper_win_requires: Recover exact original retrained-CASCADE per-cell outputs and every paper sampling/noise condition, with the original held-neuron exclusions.
Compare candidate and author models on identical fluorescence, target smoothing, alignment, edge masks and cell denominators.
Retain both glutamatergic and GABAergic cohorts; no favorable cell class, lower noise, slower target or reduced panel can define victory.
Keep source-era results and the later timing correction separate. Repairing a one-frame discrepancy is calibration, not scientific improvement.
Require meaningful correlation gain under a justified paired uncertainty rule with bias/error guardrails; new animal splits are extensions.

current_sota.description: Surpassing this source paper is distinct from current SOTA; no contemporary competitor survey or SOTA result is asserted.

episode.improvement_loop: After recovering the DS40/41 source-era configuration, iterate on declared training/development neurons while respecting each original leave-one-neuron-out exclusion. Keep all recordings and artificial-noise replicas of the test neuron out of that fit; tune denoisers and spike-rate inference only through the declared development route, with each attempt and timing convention recorded.
episode.candidate_freeze: Freeze the full glutamatergic/GABAergic roster, original sampling/noise grid and noise realizations, Gaussian target kernels, alignment and edge masks, source-era delay correction, held-neuron training exclusions, candidate parameters and budgets before final scoring. Do not select a favorable temporal shift using newly exposed final labels.
episode.final_evaluation: Evaluate candidate and recovered author models on every original held-neuron and sampling/noise condition. Preserve separate per-cell-type correlation summaries and bias/error diagnostics; retain failures and denominator changes explicitly. Lower noise, wider target smoothing, a subset of cells or the later timing repair cannot establish source-paper superiority.
episode.baseline_policy: The comparison target is the matching original retrained-CASCADE result, with cortical-default CASCADE, cross-dataset models, raw fluorescence and OASIS separately identified. Approximate default-model correlation and the modern demo’s different noise grid cannot replace the exact paper baseline. A source-era rerun and a timing-corrected rerun remain separate calibration records.

blocking_issues: Exact full numeric retrained-author baseline and original figure-producing configurations are not recovered.
Later author demo noise grid differs from the original published main comparison.
Delay correction, edge masks, random noise replicates and checkpoint training exclusions need source-era authentication.
Animal/session dependence and full original cell membership need a frozen manifest.
No qualified evaluator/rerun, justified effect threshold or fixed episode budgets.

legacy.notes: The registered runtime manifest has no qualified entrypoint or executed scientific comparison. Historical 44-cell/132-recording construction counts are not a paper win; all existing source/runtime artifacts remain calibration material.
